_comment: Read by pysimcount.figgallery. Proposed main-body figures and tables per research question (2026-11-09). A proposal for the author to accept or change, not a decision. kind: figure (path = manifest path under results/, must be a figure shown on the page), table (path = file under results/, must exist), missing (nothing to link yet; 'make' says what would produce it). status: ready = use as is; update = right content, but must be regenerated or edited for consistency (see 'todo'); missing = not generated by committed code yet. Rationale and gaps: results/gallery/main-body-selection.md.

sections.Validation: Does the pipeline reproduce the published reference (simcount, Childs et al. 2018)?
sections.RQ1: Does a low exponential count survive compilation? (cost in CNOT and T at equal precision)
sections.RQ2: How loose are the Trotter-number bounds, and does the choice of bound change the winner?
sections.RQ3: How do system size and term grouping affect r and cost per step, and does the preferred formula change?
sections.RQ4: How much do exact circuit optimisations reduce gate counts, and do they change the ranking?

items.label: V-F1
items.role: Replica of Childs et al. 2018 Fig. 13 (left): S4/S6 CNOT before and after optimisation equal simcount's published circuits at all 10 sizes.

items.label: V-T1
items.role: Parity with simcount: 119 cached cases, 117 replayed and matched exactly (same r and every gate count); the 2 Clifford+T cases need Quipper gridsynth. Generated by pfextratables.

items.label: F1a
items.role: CNOT vs n (measured n = 4-11, extrapolated to 500) with the n = 500 ranked dot plot beside it: three tiers, order inside the top tier not determined.

items.label: F1b
items.role: Same in T (Clifford+T, every extrapolated step synthesised). Same tiers; top-tier order differs from CNOT. Pair with F1a as one two-row figure. F1a/F1b now share the point rule (mean over seeds of each seed's own extrapolated count).

items.label: T1
items.role: Gain over the same-order Suzuki formula at every measured n = 4-11 (body: n = 11), geometric mean and min-max over 10 seeds; per-step ratio x r ratio checked per seed; M&O Eff prediction. Generated by pfgaintable.

items.label: T2
items.role: Sensitivity of the n = 100 and n = 500 ranking to the fit window: why F1 is read as tiers, not a winner. Main body if the n = 500 ranking is discussed at all; otherwise Limitations.

items.label: F1a
items.role: S4: bound r / measured r vs n for every bound (geometric mean, min-max over seeds, n = 4-11). tte flat at ~7x, com growing to ~95x, ana/min ~10^3, emp ~1 (not safe).

items.label: F1b
items.role: Same for S2 (the other order with all five sources of r). Pair with F1a as a two-panel figure.

items.label: T1
items.role: Bound r / measured r for every Suzuki order and bound at n = 11 (geometric mean, min-max over 10 seeds); full n = 4-11 table in np-bounds-ratio/table.md for the appendix. Generated by pfextratables from pfboundratio.

items.label: T2
items.role: Cheapest Suzuki formula under each source of r, n = 4-11, 10 seeds: S4 under measured/tte/emp at every n; S2 under min and ana at every n; com picks S2 only at n = 4. Generated by pfextratables.

items.label: F1
items.role: Mean rank over seeds vs n: answers 'does the preferred formula change with size' directly. Measured n = 4-11: M&O q=14 rank 1 on every seed; extrapolated: the top three converge.

items.label: T1
items.role: Fitted exponent b (n = 5-11, mean r; per-seed range) against 1 + 2/p and Eq. 147: same-order formulas differ (order 4: S4 1.60 vs M&O q=6 1.32), so the fits are pre-asymptotic. Generated by pfextratables.

items.label: F2
items.role: X-Y-Z vs two-group for the best formula of each family: r barely moves (ratio 1.00-1.11 at n = 10), CNOT falls 2.6-2.9x. Measured only.

items.label: T2
items.role: X-Y-Z / two-group at n = 10 (even-out, CNOT): gain = step ratio x r ratio per formula, 10/10 seeds cheaper for every formula. Two-group exists for even n only (an odd ring cannot be split into two groups). Generated by pfextratables from pfmean.

items.label: F3 (optional)
items.role: S4/S6/S8 vs n in the layout of Childs et al. 2018 Fig. 3 (right): the S4/S6 crossover (S6 cheaper from n = 30 under the n = 5-11 fit). Main body only if the crossover is discussed; otherwise appendix.

items.label: F1
items.role: Childs et al.'s 33% CNOT saving split into merging and optimiser-only (n = 13): S4 30.0% + 3.3%, S6 32.7% + 0.7%; totals equal the published 33.32%.

items.label: T1
items.role: Merging and Nam Light optimiser factors per formula at n = 11 (body; n = 4-11 in the .md), geometric mean over 10 seeds; combined CNOT factor 1.50 for every formula of order >= 2 (the 33% saving), split differently between merging and optimiser; CNOT rank unchanged by the optimiser for every formula. Generated by pfopttable.

items.label: F2
items.role: Childs et al. 2018 Fig. 13 extended to the 8 formulas of the RQ1 figures (n = 13-100; after solid/filled, before dashed/open; same colour and marker per formula as np-childs-format), r from the n = 5-11 fit: the optimiser does not change the order. n = 100 after: M&O q=14 5.90M < Blanes & Moan 5.98M < Morales m=8 6.56M.
